metadata.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
metadata.authors: Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova

nodes.name: BERT Model Architecture
nodes.statement: A multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder with $L$ layers, hidden size $H$, $A$ self-attention heads, and feed-forward size $4H$; reported in two configurations $\text{BERT}_\text{BASE}$ ($L{=}12, H{=}768, A{=}12$, 110M params) and $\text{BERT}_\text{LARGE}$ ($L{=}24, H{=}1024, A{=}16$, 340M params).
nodes.statement_clean: BERT is a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder; two sizes BASE (110M) and LARGE (340M) are reported.

nodes.name: BERT Input Representation
nodes.statement: Each input token's representation is the sum of its WordPiece token embedding (vocab size 30,000), a learned segment embedding (sentence $A$ vs $B$), and a learned position embedding; sequences begin with a classification token $\texttt{[CLS]}$ and sentence pairs are separated by $\texttt{[SEP]}$. The final hidden vector of $\texttt{[CLS]}$ is $C \in \mathbb{R}^H$ and that of token $i$ is $T_i \in \mathbb{R}^H$.
nodes.statement_clean: BERT input embedding sums WordPiece token, segment, and position embeddings, with [CLS] and [SEP] special tokens.

nodes.name: Masked Language Model (MLM) Objective
nodes.statement: A pre-training objective where 15\% of WordPiece tokens are randomly chosen for prediction; the chosen position is replaced by $\texttt{[MASK]}$ 80\% of the time, by a random token 10\% of the time, and left unchanged 10\% of the time, and the original token is predicted from the corresponding final hidden vector $T_i$ via cross-entropy loss.
nodes.statement_clean: MLM masks 15% of input tokens (with 80/10/10 mask/random/keep policy) and trains the model to predict the originals.

nodes.name: Next Sentence Prediction (NSP) Objective
nodes.statement: A binarized pre-training task: given a sentence pair $(A,B)$, with probability $1/2$ $B$ is the actual next sentence in the corpus ($\texttt{IsNext}$) and with probability $1/2$ it is a random sentence ($\texttt{NotNext}$); the $\texttt{[CLS]}$ representation $C$ is fed to a classifier predicting the binary label.
nodes.statement_clean: NSP is a binary task predicting whether sentence B truly follows sentence A, using the [CLS] vector.

nodes.name: Pre-training / Fine-tuning Framework
nodes.statement: Two-stage framework: (i) pre-train BERT on unlabeled data with MLM and NSP objectives; (ii) for each downstream task, initialize a task-specific model with the pre-trained parameters and fine-tune all parameters end-to-end with one additional output layer.
nodes.statement_clean: BERT is first pre-trained on unlabeled text (MLM+NSP) and then fine-tuned end-to-end for each downstream task.

nodes.name: WordPiece Embeddings
nodes.statement: Subword tokenization scheme producing a fixed vocabulary (here 30,000 tokens) of word pieces; rare words are split into pieces marked with $\texttt{\#\#}$.
nodes.statement_clean: WordPiece is a subword tokenizer used here with a 30k vocabulary.

nodes.name: Cloze Task
nodes.statement: Classical psycholinguistic task in which a word is deleted from a passage and the reader must restore it from surrounding context; the inspiration for the masked LM objective.

nodes.name: Transformer Encoder
nodes.statement: A stack of self-attention and position-wise feed-forward layers introduced by Vaswani et al.; BERT instantiates a multi-layer Transformer encoder with bidirectional self-attention.
nodes.origin_citation: Vaswani et al. 2017 (Attention Is All You Need)

nodes.name: BERT Pre-training Procedure
nodes.statement: Joint pre-training of a bidirectional Transformer encoder on unlabeled text using the MLM and NSP objectives.
input: Unlabeled corpus (BooksCorpus 800M words + English Wikipedia 2,500M words)
Optimizer settings: Adam, learning rate $1\mathrm{e}{-4}$, $\beta_1{=}0.9$, $\beta_2{=}0.999$, L2 weight decay $0.01$, warmup over first 10,000 steps, linear decay
Batch size 256 sequences of up to 512 tokens, 1{,}000{,}000 training steps
output: Pre-trained BERT parameters $\theta$ to initialize all downstream fine-tuning models
nodes.pseudocode: Sample two text spans (A, B) with combined length $\le 512$ tokens; with prob 1/2, B is actual next-of-A else random sentence (NSP label). Apply WordPiece tokenization; mask 15\% of token positions (80\% [MASK], 10\% random, 10\% unchanged). Compute MLM cross-entropy over masked positions plus NSP cross-entropy on $C$; sum losses; update $\theta$ via Adam.

nodes.name: BERT Fine-tuning Procedure
nodes.statement: Initialize the task model with pre-trained BERT parameters and fine-tune all parameters end-to-end on labeled data, swapping in task-specific inputs and a single new output layer.
input: Labeled task data (single sentence or sentence pair)
Task-specific output head (e.g. classification weights $W \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times H}$)
Hyperparameters: batch size $\in \{16,32\}$, learning rate $\in \{5\mathrm{e}{-5}, 3\mathrm{e}{-5}, 2\mathrm{e}{-5}\}$, epochs $\in \{2,3,4\}$, dropout $0.1$
output: Task predictions (classification logits, span scores, etc.)
nodes.pseudocode: Encode the (single or paired) input with BERT; for sequence-level tasks read out $C$ and apply $\log\,\mathrm{softmax}(C W^\top)$; for token-level tasks read out $T_i$ and apply a per-token head; back-propagate task loss through all parameters with Adam.

nodes.name: BERT SQuAD Span Prediction
nodes.statement: Fine-tune BERT to predict an answer span in a passage by introducing start and end vectors $S, E \in \mathbb{R}^H$ and scoring each position via dot products with token representations.
input: Question encoded with $A$ embeddings, passage encoded with $B$ embeddings, packed into one sequence
output: Predicted answer span $(i,j)$ with $j \ge i$ maximizing $S{\cdot}T_i + E{\cdot}T_j$ (or the no-answer span when $\hat{s}_{i,j} \le s_{\texttt{null}} + \tau$ for SQuAD 2.0)
nodes.pseudocode: Compute $P_i^{\text{start}} = \frac{e^{S\cdot T_i}}{\sum_j e^{S\cdot T_j}}$ and analogously $P_i^{\text{end}}$; train with sum of log-likelihoods of true start and end positions. For SQuAD 2.0, also compute $s_{\texttt{null}} = S\cdot C + E\cdot C$ and predict no-answer when $\hat{s}_{i,j} \le s_{\texttt{null}} + \tau$.

nodes.name: GLUE Classification Loss
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L} = -\log\,\mathrm{softmax}(C W^\top)$, where $C \in \mathbb{R}^H$ is the $\texttt{[CLS]}$ representation and $W \in \mathbb{R}^{K\times H}$ is the new classification head with $K$ class labels.

nodes.name: SQuAD Span Start Probability
nodes.statement: $P_i = \dfrac{e^{S\cdot T_i}}{\sum_j e^{S\cdot T_j}}$, the probability that token $i$ is the start of the answer span.

nodes.name: SQuAD 2.0 No-Answer Decision Rule
nodes.statement: Predict a non-null answer iff $\hat{s}_{i,j} > s_{\texttt{null}} + \tau$, where $s_{\texttt{null}} = S\cdot C + E\cdot C$ and $\hat{s}_{i,j} = \max_{j\ge i} S\cdot T_i + E\cdot T_j$, with threshold $\tau$ chosen on dev to maximize F1.

nodes.name: Bidirectional Language Representation Pre-training
nodes.statement: Learn deep bidirectional language representations from unlabeled text such that, with one additional output layer and fine-tuning, the model attains state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of sentence- and token-level NLP tasks.

nodes.name: GLUE Benchmark
nodes.statement: Suite of diverse natural-language understanding tasks (MNLI, QQP, QNLI, SST-2, CoLA, STS-B, MRPC, RTE) evaluated through a single leaderboard score.

nodes.name: SQuAD v1.1 Question Answering
nodes.statement: Given a question and a Wikipedia passage containing the answer, predict the contiguous text span in the passage that answers the question.

nodes.name: SQuAD v2.0 Question Answering with No-Answer
nodes.statement: Extension of SQuAD 1.1 that allows the question to have no answer in the provided passage; the model must either predict the answer span or abstain.

nodes.name: SWAG Grounded Commonsense Inference
nodes.statement: Given a sentence, choose the most plausible continuation among four candidate sentences; 113k examples evaluating grounded commonsense.

nodes.name: CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition
nodes.statement: Token-level sequence-tagging task: assign a named-entity label (Person, Location, Organization, Misc, O) to every token of an English news article.

nodes.name: MLM Masking Procedure on "my dog is hairy"
nodes.section: A.1 Illustration of the Pre-training Tasks
nodes.statement: With the 4-th token ("hairy") chosen for prediction: 80\% of the time replace with $\texttt{[MASK]}$ (`my dog is [MASK]'); 10\% replace with a random word (`my dog is apple'); 10\% leave unchanged (`my dog is hairy').

nodes.name: Next Sentence Prediction Pair Examples
nodes.section: A.1 Illustration of the Pre-training Tasks
nodes.statement: Positive example labeled $\texttt{IsNext}$: "[CLS] the man went to [MASK] store [SEP] he bought a gallon [MASK] milk [SEP]". Negative example labeled $\texttt{NotNext}$: "[CLS] the man [MASK] to the store [SEP] penguin [MASK] are flight \#\#less birds [SEP]".

nodes.name: GLUE Fine-tuning Results
nodes.statement: Both $\text{BERT}_\text{BASE}$ and $\text{BERT}_\text{LARGE}$ outperform all prior systems on every GLUE task, with absolute average accuracy improvements of 4.5\% and 7.0\% respectively over the previous state of the art; $\text{BERT}_\text{LARGE}$ obtains a leaderboard score of 80.5 vs. 72.8 for OpenAI GPT.

nodes.name: SQuAD v1.1 Fine-tuning Results
nodes.statement: BERT outperforms the top SQuAD 1.1 leaderboard system by $+1.5$ F1 in ensembling and $+1.3$ F1 as a single system; with TriviaQA fine-tuning data the single BERT model also exceeds the top ensemble. Test F1 reaches 93.2.

nodes.name: SQuAD v2.0 Fine-tuning Results
nodes.statement: Using the start/end + null-score thresholding rule, BERT achieves $+5.1$ F1 over the previous best system on SQuAD 2.0 (Test F1 83.1).

nodes.name: SWAG Fine-tuning Results
nodes.statement: $\text{BERT}_\text{LARGE}$ outperforms the ESIM+ELMo baseline by $+27.1\%$ and OpenAI GPT by $+8.3\%$ on SWAG.

nodes.name: Pre-training Task Ablation (No NSP, LTR & No NSP)
nodes.statement: Removing NSP significantly hurts QNLI, MNLI, and SQuAD 1.1; replacing the MLM with a left-to-right LM (LTR \& No NSP) is worse on all tasks, with large drops on MRPC and SQuAD; adding a randomly initialized BiLSTM atop the LTR model improves SQuAD but is still far below the bidirectional model.

nodes.name: Model Size Ablation
nodes.statement: Across BERT models with varying $(L, H, A)$, larger models give strictly higher Dev accuracy on MNLI, MRPC, and SST-2 — including for MRPC, which has only 3{,}600 labeled training examples and is far from the pre-training distribution; this is the first demonstration that extreme scale also helps very small downstream tasks given sufficient pre-training.

nodes.name: Feature-based Approach on CoNLL-2003 NER
nodes.statement: Using BERT activations as fixed features fed into a randomly-initialized two-layer 768-dim BiLSTM, $\text{BERT}_\text{LARGE}$ is competitive with state-of-the-art NER systems; the best variant — concatenation of the top four hidden layers — is only $0.3$ F1 behind full fine-tuning.

nodes.name: Number of Pre-training Steps Ablation
nodes.section: C.1 Effect of Number of Training Steps
nodes.statement: $\text{BERT}_\text{BASE}$ gains nearly $1.0\%$ MNLI accuracy when pre-trained for 1M steps versus 500k steps; the MLM model converges slightly slower than the LTR model in steps but outperforms it almost immediately in absolute accuracy.

nodes.name: Different Masking Procedures Ablation
nodes.section: C.2 Ablation for Different Masking Procedures
nodes.statement: Fine-tuning is robust to varying the (MASK, SAME, RND) probabilities; however the feature-based NER setting degrades sharply if the masking strategy uses only $\texttt{[MASK]}$ or only random replacement, justifying the 80/10/10 mix.

nodes.name: Why Standard Bidirectional Conditioning Fails
nodes.statement: Standard left-to-right or right-to-left LMs cannot be naively made bidirectional because doing so would let each word indirectly "see itself" through multiple layers, allowing trivial prediction; this motivates the masked-LM workaround.

nodes.name: Pre-training / Fine-tuning Mismatch
nodes.statement: The $\texttt{[MASK]}$ token never appears at fine-tuning, creating a distributional mismatch; the 80/10/10 replacement policy partially mitigates this and forces the encoder to maintain a contextual representation of every token.

nodes.name: BERT vs OpenAI GPT vs ELMo
nodes.statement: Among the three: BERT is the only deeply bidirectional model jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers; GPT is a left-to-right Transformer fine-tuning approach; ELMo concatenates independently trained left-to-right and right-to-left LSTMs and is feature-based.

nodes.name: Computational Efficiency of Fine-tuning
nodes.statement: Compared to pre-training, fine-tuning is inexpensive: every result in the paper can be reproduced in at most 1 hour on a single Cloud TPU (or a few hours on a GPU) starting from the same pre-trained checkpoint.

nodes.name: Sequence-Length Schedule for Pre-training
nodes.statement: To save compute (attention is quadratic in sequence length), pre-training uses sequence length 128 for 90\% of steps and length 512 for the remaining 10\% to learn long-range positional embeddings.

nodes.name: Sample sentence pair $(A, B)$ and assign NSP label
nodes.statement: Sample two text spans from the corpus with combined length $\le 512$ tokens; with probability $1/2$, $B$ is the actual successor of $A$ (label $\texttt{IsNext}$), else a random sentence (label $\texttt{NotNext}$).

nodes.name: WordPiece tokenize and embed with [CLS]/[SEP] and segment ids
nodes.statement: Tokenize $A$ and $B$ via WordPiece (30k vocab); prepend $\texttt{[CLS]}$, separate with $\texttt{[SEP]}$, append $\texttt{[SEP]}$; build input embedding as the sum of token, segment, and position embeddings.

nodes.name: Apply 15\% MLM masking with 80/10/10 policy
nodes.statement: Choose 15\% of token positions; for each chosen position, with probabilities $0.8/0.1/0.1$ replace with $\texttt{[MASK]}$ / a random token / leave unchanged.

nodes.name: Forward pass through bidirectional Transformer encoder
nodes.statement: Run the $L$-layer bidirectional Transformer to produce $C$ (final hidden of $\texttt{[CLS]}$) and $T_1, \ldots, T_n$ (per-token final hiddens).

nodes.name: Compute MLM + NSP loss and backpropagate
nodes.statement: Compute MLM cross-entropy on masked positions (softmax over vocabulary on $T_i$) plus NSP binary cross-entropy on $C$; sum and minimize via Adam (lr $1\mathrm{e}{-4}$, warmup 10k, linear decay) for 1M steps.

nodes.name: Initialize task model from pre-trained BERT
nodes.statement: Copy the pre-trained encoder parameters $\theta$ produced by $\text{AP224.1}$; add one task-specific output head with the few new parameters required (e.g. $W \in \mathbb{R}^{K\times H}$ for classification, or $S, E \in \mathbb{R}^H$ for span prediction).

nodes.name: Pack task input as single or paired sequence
nodes.statement: For single-sentence tasks use a degenerate pair $(\text{text}, \varnothing)$; for paired tasks (paraphrase, NLI, QA) pack the two pieces with $\texttt{[CLS]}$ and $\texttt{[SEP]}$ as in pre-training so cross-attention is bidirectional.

nodes.name: Read out [CLS] or token representations for the task head
nodes.statement: For sequence-level tasks read $C$ and apply $\log\,\mathrm{softmax}(C W^\top)$; for token-level tasks (NER, span QA) apply a head per $T_i$.

nodes.name: Fine-tune all parameters end-to-end with task loss
nodes.statement: Backpropagate the task loss into all of BERT plus the new head with Adam; sweep batch size $\in \{16, 32\}$, learning rate $\in \{5\mathrm{e}{-5}, 3\mathrm{e}{-5}, 2\mathrm{e}{-5}\}$ and epochs $\in \{2,3,4\}$ on the dev set.

nodes.name: Pack question (segment $A$) and passage (segment $B$)
nodes.statement: Encode the question with $A$ embeddings and the passage with $B$ embeddings as one packed sequence and run BERT to obtain $C$ and the per-token vectors $T_i$.

nodes.name: Score each token as a span start / end via $S, E$
nodes.statement: Compute $P_i^{\text{start}} = \frac{e^{S\cdot T_i}}{\sum_j e^{S\cdot T_j}}$ and the analogous $P_i^{\text{end}}$; train with the sum of log-likelihoods of the gold start and end positions.

nodes.name: Decode best span; for SQuAD 2.0, compare to no-answer score
nodes.statement: Predict the span $(i,j)$ with $j \ge i$ maximizing $S\cdot T_i + E\cdot T_j$; for SQuAD 2.0, predict no-answer when $\hat{s}_{i,j} \le s_{\texttt{null}} + \tau$ where $s_{\texttt{null}} = S\cdot C + E\cdot C$ and $\tau$ is tuned on the dev set.
